_doc: Per-subcategory scope-selection + read-across config for the Cat-1 compiler. Every number the compiler emits traces to a register row selected by these rules. scope_include/exclude are case-insensitive regex fragments tested against product_scope. read_across names the register row for the nearest analogous government value where no government regulates the exact product. Audited configs for rows 2-9 are filled by the build workflow; formula-powder (row 1) is the regression anchor, calibrated to reproduce the deployed, audited standard.

_read_across_canon.tHg: cn_thg_canned-complementary-foods-for-infants-a_20 — China GB 2762 total-Hg 20 for canned complementary infant foods; no government sets a mercury ML for these product forms anywhere.
_read_across_canon.Cr: china_gb2762_cr_milk_powder_2000 — China GB 2762 total-Cr 2000 for milk powder; dairy read-across. For non-dairy subcategories the nearest analogous Cr source may differ; the workflow adjudicates per subcategory.
_read_across_canon.Cr-VI: not-material: reflex speciation under total-Cr; any quantifiable Cr-VI fails.

non-root-vegetable-purees.name: Non-root vegetable purees
non-root-vegetable-purees._basis_note: Product is a wet, ready-to-eat non-root vegetable puree (jar/pouch/tub); its physical native basis is as_consumed. native_basis is deliberately set to as_sold because every applicable government limit (EU/UK/IN baby-food MLs, China canned-complementary tHg read-across) is set on this same wet product but tagged basis_class=as_sold in the register, and the compiler's 8:1 powder-reconstitution factor must NOT be applied to any of them. Setting native_basis=as_consumed makes the compiler wrongly divide those wet MLs by 8, inventing six sub-legal numbers (Pb 2.5, iAs 2.5, Cd 5, Ni 63, Sn 630, tHg 2.5) that no government sets. Trade-off: the as_sold setting instead ×8-inflates the one read-across source tagged as_consumed (AU-NZ Al) -> see Al flag.

Cr.reference_method: EPA 3060A alkaline digestion + IC-ICP-MS for Cr-VI; ICP-MS for total Cr

single-ingredient-meats.name: Single-ingredient meats (infant)
single-ingredient-meats._derivation_note: Single-ingredient infant meat/poultry purées (chicken, turkey, beef, lamb) and organ/liver. Scope pairs the US FDA processed-baby-food row (its scope enumerates 'single-ingredient meats for children under 2') with the general 'baby food' infant-food MLs. Pb therefore binds to the strictest infant-food action level (FDA 10) and iAs/Cd/Ni bind to the strictest EU infant-food MLs, whose scope ('baby food for infants and young children') covers meat-based baby food. This deliberately mirrors the sibling mixed-meals rows: a single-ingredient meat cannot carry a LOOSER limit than a mixed meal containing the same meat, so iAs is 20 (EU baby-food ML; corroborated by Israel FCS-2016 'meat and meat products, including poultry and game' iAs 20), NOT the looser China complementary-food 100. Organ/liver concentrate Cd and iAs, so holding the whole subcategory to the strictest infant-food Cd (40) and iAs (20) is the intended one-way ratchet. tHg/Sn/Al are the established baby-food read-across; Cr is not-material reflex speciation (non-dairy).

tHg.label: government read-across — Israel FCS-2016 porridges & other foods for infants and toddlers, total-Hg 8 (the strictest applicable baby-food mercury ML; supersedes the looser China canned-complementary 20).

Sn.label: government read-across (India FSSAI "Infant Milk substitute and Infant foods" Sn 5000, the only non-canned tin ML in the register) applied at face value.

Al.label: government read-across (AU-NZ Schedule 19 infant-formula Al 500, the only government aluminium ML in any jurisdiction) applied at face value; the 8:1 reconstitution factor is formula-specific and is not applied to a non-formula product.

Cr.control: No government sets a total-chromium ML for a non-dairy single-ingredient meat infant food; the only register Cr food values are dairy (China milk powder 2000, liquid milk 300) and do not transfer to a meat matrix. Cr(III) is nutritionally essential and Cr(VI) reduces to Cr(III) in a reducing meat matrix, so total-Cr is not a material toxic here. Firm control: reflex speciation — any total-Cr result > 100 ug/kg triggers Cr(VI) speciation, and any quantifiable Cr(VI) fails.
Cr.reference_method: Total-Cr screen by ICP-MS; on any result > 100 ug/kg, Cr(VI) speciation by EPA 3060A alkaline digestion + IC-ICP-MS (or EN 15192 equivalent); LOQ-level quantifiable Cr(VI) = fail.

dairy-desserts.name: Dairy-based infant desserts (yogurt, fromage frais, custard, pudding)
dairy-desserts._derivation_note: Wet, ready-to-eat dairy infant desserts (yogurt, fromage frais, custard, pudding, milk-based dessert). Scope pairs the US FDA processed-baby-food row (its scope enumerates 'yogurts; custards/puddings') with the general 'baby food' infant-food MLs. Pb binds to FDA 10; iAs/Cd/Ni to the strictest EU infant-food MLs. Chromium is MATERIAL in a dairy matrix (unlike the non-dairy Cat-1 siblings, which are not-material): it is read across to China GB 2762 liquid-milk total-Cr 300 — a basis-matched wet-dairy analogy whose register scope 'raw, pasteurized, sterilized, modified and fermented milk' covers yogurt — NOT a not-material determination. tHg/Sn/Al are the established baby-food read-across.

Cr.label: government read-across — China GB 2762 liquid-milk total-Cr 300 (scope: raw, pasteurized, sterilized, modified and fermented milk) applied at face value to a wet dairy infant dessert (basis-matched dairy analogy). Chromium IS material in a dairy matrix, so a not-material determination is not used; total Cr is a published ceiling and Cr(VI) is additionally controlled by reflex speciation (any total-Cr > 100 ppb triggers Cr(VI) speciation; any quantifiable Cr(VI) fails).

tHg.label: government read-across — Israel FCS-2016 porridges & other foods for infants and toddlers, total-Hg 8 (the strictest applicable baby-food mercury ML; stricter than the dairy-specific IL/HK milk total-Hg 10).

Sn.label: government read-across (India FSSAI "Infant Milk substitute and Infant foods" Sn 5000, the only non-canned tin ML in the register) applied at face value.

Al.label: government read-across (AU-NZ Schedule 19 infant-formula Al 500, the only government aluminium ML in any jurisdiction) applied at face value; the 8:1 reconstitution factor is formula-specific and is not applied to a non-formula product.

fish-containing-baby-food.name: Fish & seafood infant dinners
fish-containing-baby-food.development_note: SCAFFOLD — NOT certification-ready; do not publish as a standard. Purpose: give the Cat-1 mixed-meals fish-exclusion a routing destination. Fish's DEFINING hazards are methylmercury (MeHg) and inorganic/total arsenic (iAs/tAs), and neither is finished here: (1) the Cat-1 compiler panel (DEFAULT_PANEL / config.panel) does not include MeHg or tAs, so those cells are not emitted at all — the remaining work is to extend the panel for this subcategory; (2) the governing fish mercury ceiling must be derived by read-across to the Cat-6 seafood MeHg standard scaled by the dish's fish fraction — a methodology decision, not a register lookup. The 8-panel cells below resolve via DISCLOSED read-across to the nearest infant-food government values, but the total-mercury cell in particular is a baby-food PLACEHOLDER, not the fish-appropriate mercury control, and the iAs cell (China aquatic complementary 300) is a provisional aquatic-infant-food value that EU 2025/1891 fish-muscle iAs 100 may supersede once the fish-fraction basis is fixed. Remaining derivation: (a) extend the panel with MeHg + tAs for this subcategory; (b) derive the MeHg ceiling via Cat-6 read-across x fish-fraction; (c) re-derive iAs/tHg on a fish basis. Until COMPLETE + REGISTERED + CORRECTED this stays a scaffold.

Pb.label: read-across — US FDA processed-baby-food Pb action level 10 (the strictest infant-food Pb value). FDA's enumerated scope does not itemise fish dinners, so 10 is applied here as a disclosed read-across, not direct governance.

iAs.label: PROVISIONAL read-across — China GB 2762 canned complementary infant foods made from aquatic products / animal liver, iAs 300 (the nearest government iAs value for an aquatic infant complementary food). NOT final: EU 2025/1891 fish-muscle iAs 100 is a stricter fish-specific alternative; the finished fish iAs cell needs the fish-fraction derivation (see development_note).

Cd.label: read-across — EU 2023/915 baby-food / processed-cereal-based-food Cd 40 (the strictest infant-food Cd), applied to a fish-containing infant food as a disclosed read-across.

tHg.label: PLACEHOLDER read-across — China GB 2762 canned complementary infant foods total-Hg 20. This is a baby-food placeholder, NOT the fish-appropriate mercury control: fish concentrates methylmercury, and the governing ceiling must be derived from the Cat-6 seafood MeHg standard x fish fraction (in development). Do not treat this cell as final.

Ni.label: read-across — EU 2024/1987 baby-food (except juices) Ni 500, applied to a fish-containing infant food as a disclosed read-across.

Sn.label: government read-across (India FSSAI "Infant Milk substitute and Infant foods" Sn 5000, the only non-canned tin ML in the register) applied at face value.

Al.label: government read-across (AU-NZ Schedule 19 infant-formula Al 500, the only government aluminium ML in any jurisdiction) applied at face value; the 8:1 reconstitution factor is formula-specific and is not applied to a non-formula product.

Cr.control: Non-dairy fish matrix: no government sets a total-Cr ML; reflex Cr(VI) speciation on any total-Cr > 100 ug/kg, any quantifiable Cr(VI) fails.
Cr.reference_method: Total Cr by ICP-MS; reflex Cr(VI) by EPA 3060A alkaline digestion + IC-ICP-MS (or EN 15192) on any total-Cr > 100 ug/kg.

_method_note: 8:1 reconstitution applies ONLY to formula subcategories (reconstitution_8to1:true). All other subcategories take government MLs and read-across values at face value. Read-across is always face value (nearest basis-appropriate government row).
